A Spring Boot application is producing incorrect behavior.

FAILING ENDPOINT
  GET /bug/reflection-v2?type=DELIVERY&payload=alice@example.com

EXPECTED
  Delivery confirmation sent to alice@example.com
  Server log contains: [DELIVERY] Sending confirmation to: alice@example.com

OBSERVED
  HTTP 200 returned. No delivery occurs.
  Server log contains: [AUDIT] Recorded event payload: alice@example.com

No exception. No stack trace. The endpoint returns "ok".

Investigate the root cause. The application source is in:
  src/main/java/com/example/demo/
  src/main/resources/

Thought: Found it. Line 11 of `application.properties` maps `notification.handlers.delivery` to `com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler` instead of `com.example.demo.bug1.DeliveryHandler`. This causes `DELIVERY` events to be dispatched to `AuditHandler`, which logs an audit record instead of sending delivery confirmation.

**Root cause confirmed.**

The bug is in `src/main/resources/application.properties` at **line 11**:

```properties
# WRONG — maps DELIVERY events to AuditHandler
notification.handlers.delivery=com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler

# CORRECT fix
notification.handlers.delivery=com.example.demo.bug1.DeliveryHandler
```

**Why this happens:** `NotificationService2` uses `HandlerConfig` to load handler class names from properties at startup, then dispatches reflectively. Because `DELIVERY` is bound to `AuditHandler` (not `DeliveryHandler`), the audit path runs silently — no exception, no crash, just the wrong handler executing. The `alert` entry is also suspicious: it maps to `DeliveryHandler`, suggesting the two values were accidentally swapped.

The bug is in `src/main/resources/application.properties` at **line 11**.

The `delivery` and `alert` handler class names are swapped:

```properties
# BUGGY (lines 11-12)
notification.handlers.delivery=com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler
notification.handlers.alert=com.example.demo.bug1.DeliveryHandler

# FIXED
notification.handlers.delivery=com.example.demo.bug1.DeliveryHandler
notification.handlers.alert=com.example.demo.bug1.AuditHandler
```

`NotificationService2` uses `HandlerConfig` to load handler class names from properties at startup, then instantiates and invokes the handler reflectively at dispatch time (`NotificationService2.java:42-44`). Because `DELIVERY` resolves to `AuditHandler`, the audit path runs silently — returning HTTP 200 with an audit log entry, but never sending a delivery confirmation.
